title: A School Newspaper Correction
passage:
The school newspaper at Seiran Junior High published an article about the upcoming cultural festival. The article said that the drama club would perform on Saturday at two o'clock. The information came from an early planning sheet. After the newspaper had been printed, the drama club noticed that the performance had actually been moved to three o'clock.

The student editors were embarrassed. They had checked spelling and names carefully, but nobody had confirmed the final schedule. One editor suggested quietly changing the time on the online version and saying nothing about the printed mistake. Another student disagreed. Hundreds of paper copies had already been distributed, so many readers would never see the silent change.

The group decided to publish a clear correction. They placed a small notice near the school entrance, posted the corrected time online, and added a message to the morning school announcement. The next issue of the newspaper also included a short note explaining the error. The note did not blame the drama club or the student who wrote the original article. It simply stated that the newspaper had used an older schedule and should have checked the final version.

Some editors worried that admitting the mistake would make readers trust the newspaper less. Their teacher argued that the opposite could happen if corrections were handled openly. No newspaper could promise never to make an error. What mattered was how quickly mistakes were identified, corrected, and prevented from happening again.

The group changed its process. Articles about dates, prices, or schedules now had to be checked against an official source on the final editing day. One student was assigned to mark facts that could change. The system added a few minutes to production, but it reduced the chance of repeating the same type of error.

On festival day, the drama performance began at three, and the audience was full. The incorrect article did not cause a serious problem because the correction reached most readers in time. The student editors learned that accuracy is not only about being right the first time. It also includes being willing to say clearly when something was wrong and showing what will be done differently afterward.
translation:
青嵐中学校の学校新聞は文化祭の記事で、演劇部の上演が土曜日の二時からだと掲載しました。その情報は初期の計画表から取ったものでした。印刷後、演劇部から実際には三時へ変更されていると連絡がありました。

編集部は恥ずかしく感じました。名前や誤字はよく確認したのに、最終日程を確認していなかったのです。オンライン版だけ黙って直そうという意見も出ましたが、紙はすでに何百部も配られており、多くの読者には修正が届きません。

そこで学校入口へ訂正掲示を出し、オンライン版を直し、朝の校内放送でも正しい時刻を知らせました。次号には短い訂正文を載せ、演劇部や記事を書いた生徒を責めず、『古い日程を使い、最終版確認が不足していた』と説明しました。

間違いを認めると新聞への信頼が下がるのではと心配する生徒もいました。しかし先生は、公開して直す方が信頼につながる場合があると言いました。絶対に間違えない新聞はありません。重要なのは、間違いをどれだけ早く見つけ、直し、同じことを防ぐかです。

その後、日付、料金、時刻など変わり得る情報は最終編集日に公式資料と照合し、変更可能な事実に印を付ける担当も決めました。作業は少し増えましたが、同じ種類の失敗を減らせます。

文化祭当日、演劇は三時から満員の観客の前で始まりました。訂正が間に合ったため大きな混乱はありませんでした。編集部は、正確さとは最初から正しいことだけではなく、間違った時には明確に認め、その後どう変えるか示すことも含むと学びました。
